hook: *75* PAANI complaints: people mopping floors with drinking water
hook_b: *75* PAANI complaints: people mopping floors with drinking water
tldr: Over 250 complaints came in on the water board's PAANI app in four weeks; about 75 were about residents mopping floors with drinking water or groundwater.

beats.what: PAANI, launched on Oct 29, lets residents photograph and report misuse of drinking water across 10 categories.
beats.why: HMWSSB says the city's water reserves are in a critical state and wants potable water kept for drinking and cooking.
beats.care: Fines run from ₹1,000 to ₹20,000; unpaid penalties get added to the water bill.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Most floor-mopping complaints came from Jubilee Hills and Banjara Hills, officials said; field teams found pressure motors on drinking-water lines used to wash floors and driveways.

cards.q: Should water-wasting fines show up on your water bill?

qs: Would residents switch to treated STP water for cleaning if it were piped to homes?

facts.t: The PAANI app has *1,000+* downloads and about *700* active users.

viz.verdict: Floor-mopping with drinking water is the most-flagged misuse.

watch: Whether HMWSSB pushes treated STP water for floor cleaning, gardening and construction.
